info.title: Frappé API
info.description: The operating system for restaurants and cafés in Latin America. Version 1 is anonymous and rate limited per client; its administration writes are not authenticated yet. Texts follow Accept-Language and Content-Language names the languages served; every endpoint declares its caching, and cacheable answers carry strong ETags; every error is an RFC 9457 Problem Details with a stable code.

get.description: Every ISO 3166-1 country, ordered by code, with its codes, its name and its currencies in use. Names answer in the language of Accept-Language: the requested tag, then its base language, any Portuguese in pt-BR, then English. Content-Language names the languages served.

parameters.name: Accept-Language
parameters.description: The languages the client accepts (BCP 47, with q weights). Frappé is written in en, es, es-AR, es-MX, pt-BR; the ranges are tried from the highest quality down and the first one served wins (fr, es-AR;q=0.8 answers in es-AR). Another Spanish answers in es, any Portuguese in pt-BR, and anything else, or no header, in English. Content-Language names the language served.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: ETags of the copies the client holds (or *): when one matches, the answer is 304 without a body.

Content-Language.description: The languages Frappé's own texts in the response are written in; absent when it holds none, only proper nouns, identifiers and source data (names and categories as their source publishes them).

ETag.description: Strong validator of this representation, language included; send it back in If-None-Match.

Cache-Control.description: public, max-age=86400 at most (seconds); some answers expire sooner, such as time zones before an offset change.

Vary.description: Accept-Language: each language is a separate representation with its own ETag; a cache keys on it.

Content-Language.description: The languages the problem's texts are written in.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before the client's window reopens (also in the error's parameters.retryAfter).

CountryResponse.description: A country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, alpha-3 and numeric codes, its name, and its currencies in order of preference.

CurrencyResponse.description: A currency: ISO 4217 code, CLDR name and standard symbol (same language), and its minor unit digits.

examples.title: The resource does not exist.
examples.detail: The URL does not match any endpoint of the API.

errors.message: The URL does not match any endpoint of the API.

type.description: The category of the failure: urn:frappe:problem: and a stable slug. It never names an error code.

title.description: Stable summary of the category, in the language of Content-Language.

detail.description: The error's text when there is one, or how many errors there are, in the language of Content-Language.

errors.description: Every error found, so a client can fix them all at once.

traceId.description: W3C trace id of the request, to find it in the logs and traces.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 Problem Details. type is the category of the failure; the error codes are only in errors, which always lists every error, one or several.

parameters.description: The values the error was raised with, by name (the same the texts use).

message.description: The error in the language of Content-Language; absent when no text exists.

ProblemError.description: One error: its stable code, the values it was raised with and its text in the response language.
